Remark Scope of the far-commuting minimality theorem.

Scope

This theorem elevates the mathematical content of the selection principle to a proved statement. It does not assert that the electroweak sector is this set of links; that identification remains a conjectural input. The far-commuting bound and enumeration provide the facts upon which that postulate operates.
conj:electroweak-higgs-torus-link-triple:
Conjecture (W^\pm, Z, H) \leftrightarrow (T(2,4), T(2,6), T(2,8)) — non-Bring even-twist 2-component torus-link triplet. In any QOU built on Bring's surface with EM/strong sector \{T_{2,9}, T_{3,5}\}, the standard-model electroweak gauge bosons W^\pm, Z and the Higgs scalar H correspond to the three even-twist 2-component torus links of the sub-saturating complement:

  W^{\pm} \;\longleftrightarrow\; T(2,4),
  \qquad
  Z \;\longleftrightarrow\; T(2,6),
  \qquad
  H \;\longleftrightarrow\; T(2,8).

This is the top of the electroweak chain of conjectures. Its provable base — that these three links exist, have Seifert genera 1, 2, 3, co-embed in Bring's genus-4 fiber alongside the saturating carriers, and fit minimally in B_6 at the far-commuting triple (1,3,5) — is proved. What remains conjectural is the identification itself. Charge and spin are proved consequences of a single sector postulate.

C1 — the selection principle.

The electroweak carriers are the nontrivial, strictly sub-saturating even-twist 2-component torus links. Their Seifert genus g lies in the window 0 < g < 4 = g(\Sigma_4). This forms the sub-saturating complement of the genus-4 saturating force-carrier knots \{T_{2,9}, T_{3,5}\}. These two are the only coprime solutions of (p-1)(q-1) = 8, exhausting Bring's genus-4 capacity. The Hopf link T(2,2) (genus 0) is the trivial endpoint and is excluded. The saturation mechanism that forces \{T_{2,9}, T_{3,5}\} for the strong carriers selects the sub-saturating window for the weak carriers.

C2 — enumeration.

Given C1, the carrier window 0 < g < 4 contains exactly the genera 1, 2, 3 (k \in \{2, 3, 4\}): the triplet T(2,4), T(2,6), T(2,8). The forward inclusion is a provable enumeration. The conjectural content of C2 is the reverse inclusion: all three genera are realised as carriers.

C_{\text{sector}} — the single sector-assignment postulate.

Charge and spin are unified by one \mathbb{Z}/2 datum: the assignment of each carrier to a sector of the spin involution \sigma, A = A_+ \oplus A_-. Restricted to the sym/alt Hecke block, \sigma is the swap of the eigenvalues q^{2k} \leftrightarrow q^{-2k}. Its projections give a bar-even part in A_+ (neutral, retained by the Markov trace) and a bar-odd part in A_- (charged, traceless). The Higgs is the bar-even self-dual carrier.

Given the sector assignment (H singlet, W^\pm, Z doublets), spin and charge follow. H \in A_+ implies scalar (spin 0) and neutral. W^\pm \in A_- implies vector (spin 1) with T_3 = \pm 1. Z \in A_- implies vector, neutral with T_3 = 0 via the (W^3, B) \mapsto (Z, \gamma) Weinberg mixing. The remaining conjectural input is the sector assignment itself.

The \sigma_5^8 bar-grading is derived from spin.

The Weinberg-angle block reads the Hoefsmit slot \sigma_5^8 as the \mathrm{U}(1)_Y hypercharge gauge boson B. This block reads \sigma_5^8 (= T(2,8), strands 5–6) as the Higgs. There is no conflict: \sigma_5^8 carries both, bar-graded by the spin involution. The Higgs boson H is the A_+ (bar-even, scalar) part. The hypercharge gauge boson B is the A_- (bar-odd, vector) part.

This bar-grading is derived from the two carriers' spins. The sector\tospin map is injective and inverts. Spin determines the sector. The Higgs is a scalar and B a vector as independent physical inputs, so H \in A_+ and B \in A_- are forced. The residual postulate is that both H and B inhabit the one \sigma_5^8 slot. The self-dual figure-eight 4_1 is the Higgs mass mechanism, not the 125\,GeV Higgs boson. The boson is the electroweak-slot link T(2,8) = A_+ of \sigma_5^8.

The W vs Z slot assignment is a free label.

Spin fixes each carrier's sector (scalar H \to A_+; vectors W, Z \to A_-). It does not fix which of the two A_- vector slots is the charged W^\pm and which is the neutral Z. The crossing-to-charge map Q = \tfrac12\,\mathrm{writhe} on the all-positive braid \sigma_1^{2k} gives Q(T(2,2k)) = k > 0 for all three carriers. It cannot single out the neutral slot. The assignment W = \sigma_1^4 relies on the mass ordering 4 < 6 < 8. Both W = \sigma_1^4 and the mirror W = \sigma_3^6 satisfy every proved constraint.

Supporting evidence.

  1. Mass ordering. The standard-model ordering m_{W^\pm} < m_Z < m_H maps monotonically onto the crossing-number ordering 4 < 6 < 8.
  2. PSD-feasibility probe. An exploratory SDP-feasibility probe shows PSD discrimination. Among the candidates tested, only the even-twist torus links, here the triplet \{T(2,4), T(2,6), T(2,8)\}, produced positive-semidefinite Hecke certificates on every Wedderburn block.

thm:hoefsmit-ew-cell-content:
Theorem Hoefsmit cell content of the far-commuting triple (\sigma_1, \sigma_3, \sigma_5): disjoint strand pairs and eight pure-pattern idempotents. Let R be a commutative ring in which q and [2]_q = q + q^{-1} are invertible, and let \sigma_1, \sigma_3, \sigma_5 be three pairwise-commuting elements of a commutative R-algebra, each satisfying the Hecke relation \sigma^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma + 1. Write e^{s}(\sigma) = (\sigma + q^{-1})/[2]_q (the symmetric idempotent, eigenvalue q) and e^{a}(\sigma) = (q - \sigma)/[2]_q (the antisymmetric idempotent, eigenvalue -q^{-1}), and for \epsilon_1, \epsilon_2, \epsilon_3 \in \{s, a\} set

  E(\epsilon_1, \epsilon_2, \epsilon_3) \;:=\; e^{\epsilon_1}(\sigma_1)\, e^{\epsilon_2}(\sigma_3)\, e^{\epsilon_3}(\sigma_5).

Then:

  1. (Disjoint strand pairs.) The strand pairs \{1,2\}, \{3,4\}, \{5,6\} on which \sigma_1, \sigma_3, \sigma_5 act are pairwise disjoint and their union is \{1, \dots, 6\}.
  2. (Pure-pattern idempotents.) The eight elements E(\epsilon_1, \epsilon_2, \epsilon_3) are idempotent and pairwise orthogonal, and their sum is 1.
  3. (Six-pattern decomposition.) The six patterns other than (s,s,s) and (a,a,a) satisfy 
      \sum_{(\epsilon_1, \epsilon_2, \epsilon_3) \neq (s,s,s),\,(a,a,a)} E(\epsilon_1, \epsilon_2, \epsilon_3) \;=\; 1 - E(s,s,s) - E(a,a,a).
  4. (Closure invariants of the carrier powers.) For k = 2, 3, 4, the word \sigma^{2k} in the braid group B_2 of a single strand pair induces the identity permutation of the strand endpoints, so its closure has two components, and its writhe is 2k.

Computed tableau multiplicities

Enumerating the 76 standard Young tableaux of size 6 and classifying each of \sigma_1, \sigma_3, \sigma_5 on the Hoefsmit seminormal basis vector as sym, alt or mixed gives exactly 20 tableaux on which all three act diagonally. Their sym/alt patterns occur with multiplicities

(s,s,s) (a,s,s) (s,a,s) (s,s,a) (a,a,s) (a,s,a) (s,a,a) (a,a,a)
4 2 1 3 3 1 2 4

These counts are computed (by enumerating standard tableaux and eigenvalue classes); they are not derived in closed form.

The naming of the six patterns and of the carrier powers \sigma_1^4, \sigma_3^6, \sigma_5^8 as the electroweak carriers W, Z, H, together with the minimality of n = 6, the interface-knot refinement, the dimension-collapse resolution, the Plancherel-weight special case and the N_v implication, is collected in the Hoefsmit cell-content context.
rem:hoefsmit-ew-cell-content-context:
Remark Electroweak naming, minimality, interface-knot refinement, and further structure of the Hoefsmit electroweak cell content.

Naming: the electroweak carriers

The three carrier powers of the Hoefsmit cell content are named after the electroweak force-carriers:

  W \;\longleftrightarrow\; \sigma_1^{\,4} \;\;(\text{strands 1--2}),
  \quad
  Z \;\longleftrightarrow\; \sigma_3^{\,6} \;\;(\text{strands 3--4}),
  \quad
  H \;\longleftrightarrow\; \sigma_5^{\,8} \;\;(\text{strands 5--6}),

and the six patterns other than (s,s,s) and (a,a,a) are named by the carriers whose idempotent is antisymmetric: (a,s,s), (s,a,s) and (s,s,a) are the W, Z and H patterns, and (a,a,s), (a,s,a) and (s,a,a) are the WZ, WH and ZH patterns. These labels carry no charge assignment. On its own strand pair the carrier \sigma^{2k}, k = 2, 3, 4, closes to a two-component link of writhe 2k, and in the standard braid presentation of torus links that closure is the torus link T(2, 2k); so the carriers are read as T(2,4), T(2,6), T(2,8) on Bring's surface. This is a naming of constructions. That these links are the physical W^\pm, Z and H is the electroweak/Higgs torus-link identification. It is not used by the theorem.

Minimality of n = 6

Each EW carrier acts on a single strand-pair. Three carriers need three disjoint strand-pairs. For n < 6, carriers share strand-pairs, their generators no longer commute, and the simultaneous-eigenspace decomposition degenerates.

Refinement: coupling via interface knot

The disjoint-product framing treats W, Z, H as independent. The corrected EW braid uses an interface knot \bowtie_K \in H_6(q) to mediate the coupling, analogous to the inter-nucleon interface in the deuteron derivation. The corrected braid is:

  \beta_{\rm EW}(\bowtie_K)
  \;:=\;
  \sigma_1^{\,4} \cdot \bowtie_K^{(W \to Z)} \cdot \sigma_3^{\,6}
  \cdot \bowtie_K^{(Z \to H)} \cdot \sigma_5^{\,8} \cdot \bowtie_K^{(H \to W)}.

This modifies pattern multiplicities, impacts bar-self-duality, gives the Higgs-vev automorphism a concrete form, and twists the 8 pure patterns.

Resolution of the dimension-collapse issue

On the 20 standard tableaux of size 6 on which \sigma_1, \sigma_3, \sigma_5 all act diagonally, the six EW patterns W, Z, H, WZ, WH, ZH occur with tableau multiplicities 2, 1, 3, 3, 1, 2, and the two non-EW patterns, the vacuum (s,s,s) and the fully broken (a,a,a), with multiplicity 4 each. These are counts of tableaux, not ranks. The six EW patterns sit alongside the two non-EW patterns, resolving the dimension-collapse issue of the H_2(q)-only completeness sum.

The Plancherel weight is a degenerate special case

The earlier Plancherel-weighted multiplier framing is incorrect. The structural multiplier is the direct unweighted trace \mathrm{tr}_{\rm pure} over the pure seminormal vectors, which preserves bar-self-duality automatically from the disjoint-strand-pair construction.

Implication for N_v derivation

The constrained-PSLQ basis for N_v must use the direct cell-content trace \mathrm{tr}_{\rm pure} as the structural input, demoting the Plancherel framing to a degenerate special case.

Historical alignment: quaternionic electroweak theory

The disjoint-strand-pair identification parallels Morita's quaternionic formulation of the Weinberg–Salam theory [morita1982]. The QOU tetraplectic boundary supplies a geometric home for the \mathrm{SU}(2) structures. The unit-quaternion actions are norm-preserving and commute; identifying these algebraic actions with physical carriers is an interpretive alignment, not a derivation.

thm:ew-triplet-charge-spin-from-involuti:
Theorem Sector label and charge of the electroweak triplet computed through the spin involution. Conditional on the electroweak sector-selection postulate. Let R be a field with \tfrac{1}{2} \in R, and let \sigma be the spin involution, acting on the two-dimensional sym/alt block of the electroweak Hoefsmit cells as the swap \sigma(x, y) = (y, x). Assume the sector-selection postulate: each electroweak carrier c lies in the \sigma-even sector A_+ or the \sigma-odd sector A_-, with H \in A_+ (the self-dual Higgs carrier) and W^\pm, Z \in A_-; c has carrier eigenvalue a_c = q^{2k} \in R^\times with a_c^2 \neq 1; and a_{W^-} = a_{W^+}^{-1}, so that W^- carries the \sigma-image of W^+. Let v_c be the \sigma-even projection of (a_c, a_c^{-1}) if c \in A_+ and its \sigma-odd projection if c \in A_-. Define the sector label 2s(c) = 0 if \sigma v_c = v_c and 2s(c) = 2 otherwise, and the charge Q(c) = \mathrm{skew}(v_c), where \mathrm{skew}(x, y) = x - y. Then

  2s(H) = 0, \qquad 2s(W^\pm) = 2s(Z) = 2,
  Q(H) = 0, \qquad Q(W^+) \neq 0, \qquad Q(W^-) = -Q(W^+).

Both the sector label and the charge are computed from the action of \sigma on the sector vectors v_c.

The label 2s is a two-valued sector label of the model, named "spin" because A_+ is read as scalar and A_- as vector; it is not a computation of Lorentz spin. The sectors A_\pm are the two one-dimensional \mathbb{Z}/2-sectors of \sigma, not spin multiplets.

The theorem does not assign isospin. The paper's table 2T_3(W^\pm) = \pm 1, 2T_3(Z) = 2T_3(H) = 0 (so T_3(W^\pm) = \pm\tfrac12, the doublet values of the spin involution, not the triplet values \pm 1) is recorded, not derived from \sigma, and it is not a function of Q of the form \lambda Q + \mu: the row H forces \mu = 0, the row Z forces \lambda = 0 because Q(Z) \neq 0, and the row W^+ then fails. The normalised charge Q(c)/Q(W^+) takes the values 1, -1, 0 on W^+, W^-, H and a nonzero value on Z. The spin-involution rule, 2T_3 = 0 on A_+ and 2T_3 = \pm 1 on A_-, with the sign read as the sign of Q over an ordered field with a_{W^+}, a_Z > 1, gives 2T_3(H) = 0, 2T_3(W^\pm) = \pm 1 and 2T_3(Z) = 1. Each reading agrees with the table except at Z. In particular T_3(H) = 0 is a consequence of H \in A_+ under that rule, not an input of this theorem.

The \sigma-parity alone gives Q(Z) \neq 0, since Z \in A_-. Weinberg mixing does not repair this for a linear charge. Write Z = cW^3 - sB and \gamma = sW^3 + cB with c^2 + s^2 = 1, and extend Q linearly from x = Q(W^3) and y = Q(B). Then Q(Z)^2 + Q(\gamma)^2 = x^2 + y^2, so Q(Z) = Q(\gamma) = 0 holds only if x = y = 0. If W^3 and B are \sigma-odd sector vectors with non-degenerate eigenvalues, as the \sigma_5^8 grading places B, then x \neq 0 and no angle makes both Z and \gamma neutral.

Interpretation. In the Standard Model W^3 and B both carry zero electric charge, and that is why Z and \gamma are both neutral; the rotation does not create neutrality. The model's T_3(H) = 0 differs from the Standard Model, where the neutral component of the Higgs doublet has T_3 = -\tfrac{1}{2}.
prf:ew-triplet-charge-spin-from-involuti:
Proof Bar-parity of the even-twist carriers and the forced quantum numbers.

The provable half — bar-parity of the even-twist carriers

The even-twist carrier T(2,2k) occupies the two-dimensional sym/alt Hecke block with eigenvalues (q^{2k}, q^{-2k}). The spin involution acts on this block as the swap \sigma(x,y) = (y,x). This is precisely the bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1} sending q^{2k} \leftrightarrow q^{-2k}. Its projections split the carrier:

  1. bar-even part a_+ \in A_+, \sigma-fixed, with neutral (Markov-trace) value q^{2k} + q^{-2k}.
  2. bar-odd part a_- \in A_-, \sigma-negated, traceless with nonzero skew value q^{2k} - q^{-2k}.

The Higgs is the bar-even, self-dual, real-volume carrier; the W^\pm and Z are bar-odd.

The computed sector label and charge

Let v_c be the sector vector of the carrier c: the \sigma-even projection of (a_c, a_c^{-1}) if c \in A_+, and its \sigma-odd projection if c \in A_-. If c \in A_+, then v_c is \sigma-fixed, so 2s(c) = 0, and its skew value is 0, so Q(c) = 0. If c \in A_-, then \sigma v_c = -v_c. Since 2 is invertible and a_c^2 \neq 1, v_c \neq 0, hence \sigma v_c \neq v_c and 2s(c) = 2; its skew value is a_c - a_c^{-1} \neq 0, so Q(c) \neq 0. For W^-, the eigenvalue is a_{W^+}^{-1}, so Q(W^-) = -Q(W^+). With H \in A_+ and W^\pm, Z \in A_- this gives the statement.

The postulated data are the sector map and the eigenvalues. The isospin table T_3 is recorded, not derived. The \sigma-parity alone makes Z charged, since Z \in A_-.

Isospin and mixing against the charge

If 2T_3(c) = \lambda Q(c) + \mu for all four carriers, then H gives \mu = 0 since Q(H) = 0; Z gives \lambda Q(Z) = 0, so \lambda = 0 since Q(Z) \neq 0; and W^+ gives 1 = 0. Over an ordered field, a > 1 gives a^{-1} < 1 < a, so a - a^{-1} > 0. Hence Q(W^+), Q(Z) > 0 and Q(W^-) = -Q(W^+) < 0, and the signs of Q are 0, 1, -1, 1 on H, W^+, W^-, Z.

For the rotation Z = cW^3 - sB, \gamma = sW^3 + cB with c^2 + s^2 = 1 and a linear charge with x = Q(W^3), y = Q(B):

  c\,Q(Z) + s\,Q(\gamma) = (c^2 + s^2)\,x = x,
  \qquad
  -s\,Q(Z) + c\,Q(\gamma) = (c^2 + s^2)\,y = y.

So Q(Z) = Q(\gamma) = 0 forces x = y = 0, and Q(Z)^2 + Q(\gamma)^2 = x^2 + y^2. With c = \cot\theta_W \cdot s, one has Q(Z) = s(\cot\theta_W \cdot x - y), which for s \neq 0 vanishes exactly when \cot\theta_W \cdot x = y.

The \sigma_5^8 bar-grading is derived from spin

The Weinberg-angle block reads the Hoefsmit slot \sigma_5^8 as the \mathrm{U}(1)_Y hypercharge gauge boson B. The triplet block reads \sigma_5^8 (= T(2,8), strands 5–6) as the Higgs. There is no conflict: \sigma_5^8 carries both, bar-graded by the spin involution. The Higgs boson H is the A_+ (bar-even, scalar) part; the hypercharge gauge boson B is the A_- (bar-odd, vector) part.

This bar-grading follows from the two carriers' sector labels. The map from sector to label is injective and inverts, so the label determines the sector. Reading the Higgs as scalar and B as vector, as independent inputs, forces H \in A_+ and B \in A_-. The residual postulate is that both H and B inhabit the one \sigma_5^8 slot.
rem:ew-triplet-charge-spin-slot-assignme:
Remark The W vs Z slot assignment is a free label.

The W vs Z slot assignment is a free label

The sector membership A_+ / A_- of each carrier is forced by its spin. A charged carrier must be a bar-odd A_- doublet. What is not forced is which of the two vector slots — \sigma_1^4 or \sigma_3^6 — hosts the charged W^\pm versus the neutral Z. The crossing\tocharge map Q = \tfrac12\,\mathrm{writhe} on the all-positive braid \sigma_1^{2k} gives Q(T(2,2k)) = k > 0 for every carrier. It cannot single out the neutral slot. The surviving \mathrm{writhe} \to I_3 map assigns 2 I_3 = 2k, nonzero on both vector slots. No proved crossing\tocharge principle selects the W slot: both W = \sigma_1^4 and the mirror W = \sigma_3^6 satisfy every proved constraint.

The signed charge-conjugation test

Charge conjugation is crossing reversal. The operation C = (\sigma \leftrightarrow \sigma^{-1}) reverses every crossing. Within the even-twist slot family \sigma_1^{2k} \subset B_2 — all carriers presented at the same strand number — a carrier is neutral iff it is a fixed point of C, i.e. C-invariant or amphichiral, and over \mathbb{Z} this fixed-point condition is exactly the vanishing of the signed writhe. The restriction to a fixed level is required: the writhe is not a function of the link, so the unknot presented as \sigma_1^{\pm 1} has nonzero writhe without being charged. The argument below compares slots at n = 2 throughout and is unaffected.

Admitting the signed asymmetry does not force which slot is W: two distinct signed labelings both satisfy the full C-invariance neutrality constraint yet disagree on the charged slot. The signed test constrains the neutral slot to be amphichiral, but not which slot it is.

prf:ew-slot-far-commutation-obstruction:
Proof The far-commuting slots cannot carry the non-abelian bracket. The slot indices 1, 3, 5 are pairwise far apart. Thus \sigma_1, \sigma_3, \sigma_5 pairwise commute. Consequently, the subalgebra \mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{slot}} = \langle \sigma_1, \sigma_3, \sigma_5 \rangle is commutative. Every commutator \lbrack x, y \rbrack = xy - yx vanishes for x, y \in \mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{slot}}. The three carriers W \leftrightarrow \sigma_1^{4}, Z \leftrightarrow \sigma_3^{6}, H \leftrightarrow \sigma_5^{8} pairwise commute.

The obstruction is the incompatibility of two facts:

  1. Commuting operators have vanishing bracket. For x, y \in \mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{slot}}, \lbrack x, y \rbrack = 0.
  2. The \mathfrak{su}(2)_L adjoint is non-abelian. Its generators satisfy \lbrack J_a, J_b \rbrack = \varepsilon_{abc} J_c \ne 0. A nonzero bracket forbids commutation.

If both J_1, J_2 \in \mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{slot}}, then \lbrack J_1, J_2 \rbrack = 0 by (1), contradicting J_3 \ne 0 by (2). At least one \mathfrak{su}(2)_L generator must escape the slot subalgebra. \square

prop:higgs-vacuum-residual-idempotent:
Proposition The vacuum idempotent e = t^{-1}\varrho\varrho^{*}, its residual, and the symmetric split of \mathrm{id} - e \otimes e. Let \mathbf{C} be a K-linear category over a field K, let U, X be objects, and let

  \varrho \colon U \to X, \qquad \varrho^{*} \colon X \to U, \qquad
  \varrho^{*} \circ \varrho \;=\; t \cdot \mathrm{id}_U, \quad t \in K^{\times}

be a point / copoint pair with invertible pairing. Define

  e \;:=\; t^{-1}\, \varrho \circ \varrho^{*} \colon X \to X,
  \qquad
  r \;:=\; \mathrm{id}_X - e .

(a) Vacuum idempotent and residual.

  1. e \circ e = e, \;e \circ \varrho = \varrho, \;\varrho^{*} \circ e = \varrho^{*}.
  2. r \circ r = r, \;e \circ r = r \circ e = 0, \;e + r = \mathrm{id}_X.
  3. r \circ \varrho = 0 and \varrho^{*} \circ r = 0: the residual annihilates the vacuum.

(b) Symmetric / antisymmetric split of the two-vacuum residual. Let \sigma \colon Y \to Y satisfy \sigma \circ \sigma = \mathrm{id}_Y and let c \in K with c + c = 1 (so \operatorname{char} K \neq 2 and c = \tfrac12). Put P_{+} = c\,(\mathrm{id}_Y + \sigma) and P_{-} = c\,(\mathrm{id}_Y - \sigma). Then P_\pm are idempotent, P_{+} + P_{-} = \mathrm{id}_Y, P_{-} \circ P_{+} = 0, \sigma \circ P_{+} = P_{+}, \sigma \circ P_{-} = -P_{-}, and P_\pm commute with every endomorphism that commutes with \sigma.

Now let \mathbf{C} be symmetric monoidal and monoidal-preadditive, Y = X \otimes X, \sigma = \beta_{X,X}, and let R := \mathrm{id}_{X \otimes X} - e \otimes e be the residual of the two-vacuum idempotent. Then:

  1. e \otimes e and R are idempotent, and both commute with P_{\pm} (naturality of \beta).
  2. R = P_{+} \circ R + P_{-} \circ R, where P_{\pm} \circ R are idempotents and (P_{-} \circ R) \circ (P_{+} \circ R) = 0.
  3. R = r \otimes e + e \otimes r + r \otimes r.
  4. P_{+} \circ (r \otimes r) is an idempotent: the symmetric square of the residual.

(c) Traces. Let \mathrm{tr} assign to each endomorphism a scalar in K, additively, K-homogeneously and cyclically: \mathrm{tr}(g \circ f) = \mathrm{tr}(f \circ g) for f \colon Y \to Z, g \colon Z \to Y. Then

  1. \mathrm{tr}(e) = \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_U) and \mathrm{tr}(r) = \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_X) - \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_U). In particular, for U = \mathbf{1} and \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{1}}) = 1, \mathrm{tr}(e) = 1, whatever X is.

Items 1–7 use no rigidity, trace or pivotal structure. Item 8 takes the trace as a hypothesis with the three stated properties; it does not construct the pivotal trace of a particular category. In a rigid category \varrho^{*} would come from \varrho through a self-duality of X; the statements above need only the scalar identity \varrho^{*} \circ \varrho = t \cdot \mathrm{id}_U.

Proof. Each item is a short computation. For example, e \circ e = t^{-2}\,\varrho\,(\varrho^{*}\varrho)\,\varrho^{*} = t^{-2} t\,\varrho\varrho^{*} = e. For P_{+}: (\mathrm{id} + \sigma)^2 = 2(\mathrm{id} + \sigma), so P_{+}^2 = c^2 \cdot 2(\mathrm{id} + \sigma) = c(c+c)(\mathrm{id} + \sigma) = P_{+}. Item 5 is the general fact that commuting idempotents compose to an idempotent. Item 8: \mathrm{tr}(e) = t^{-1}\,\mathrm{tr}(\varrho \circ \varrho^{*}) = t^{-1}\,\mathrm{tr}(\varrho^{*} \circ \varrho) = t^{-1}\,\mathrm{tr}(t\,\mathrm{id}_U) = \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_U). Item 6 follows from \mathrm{id}_{X\otimes X} = (e + r) \otimes (e + r) and bilinearity of \otimes.
conj:g-action-on-aether:
Conjecture Categorical G = \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{U}(1)_Y action on the Frobenius–Hopf aether. The proposal is that the Frobenius–Hopf aether A in \mathbf{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) admits a unique G-equivariant structure under G = \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{U}(1)_Y. This structure is governed by four constraints linking the categorical data to the electroweak sector. The constraints are intended to give the symmetric-channel Frobenius trace \mathcal{N}_{\rm sym}(q) = \mathrm{tr}_F(e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW} \cdot e_H) in closed form. The closed form depends on how the trace composes across the hosts, which is not yet fixed (see below).

The four constraints

Constraint (G-1) — G-isotypic decomposition. The aether A decomposes as a direct sum of G-isotypic components:

  A \;=\; A^{(\gamma)} \;\oplus\; A^{(W^+)} \;\oplus\; A^{(W^-)}
  \;\oplus\; A^{(Z)} \;\oplus\; A^{(H)} \;\oplus\; A^{(\rm matter)}

where each A^{(X)} carries a unique irreducible representation of G. See Table 1.

Constraint (G-2) — Per-host q-dimension assignment. The categorical q-dimension of each component is determined by its torus-link host:

  \dim_q\bigl(A^{(W^\pm)}\bigr) \;=\; [4]_q,
  \qquad
  \dim_q\bigl(A^{(Z)}\bigr) \;=\; [6]_q,
  \qquad
  \dim_q\bigl(A^{(H)}\bigr) \;=\; [2]_q.

The W-host scale [4]_q reflects the T(2,4) crossing count, and the Z-host scale [6]_q reflects T(2,6). The Higgs scale [2]_q is the q-dimension of the fundamental representation, restricted to the neutral component.

Constraint (G-3) — Higgs vacuum vortex morphism. The Higgs vacuum value \langle\Phi\rangle \in A is a non-zero vortex morphism \varrho_\Phi \colon \mathbf{1} \to A^{(H)}, unique up to a non-zero scalar, satisfying

  Q \cdot \varrho_\Phi = 0, \qquad
  \mathrm{tr}_F(\varrho_\Phi^* \cdot \varrho_\Phi) = v^2 / m_e^2,

where Q = T_3 + Y is the unbroken charge generator and v \approx 246\,\mathrm{GeV} is the weak vacuum expectation value. The first condition forces neutrality under the unbroken \mathrm{U}(1)_{\text{em}} and, when the neutral subspace of A^{(H)} is one-dimensional, fixes \varrho_\Phi up to a non-zero scalar. The second fixes the modulus of that scalar to the empirical Higgs VEV and leaves its phase free, so \varrho_\Phi is unique only up to a phase. The idempotent e_H of (G-4) does not depend on that phase.

Constraint (G-4) — Higgs idempotent. The categorical Higgs idempotent e_H is defined from \varrho_\Phi by:

  e_H \;=\; \frac{\varrho_\Phi \cdot \varrho_\Phi^*}{\mathrm{tr}_F(\varrho_\Phi^* \cdot \varrho_\Phi)}.

This rank-1 projector isolates the unbroken 1-dimensional subspace of A^{(H)}. Its trace is

  \mathrm{tr}_F(e_H) \;=\; 1.

The idempotent factors through the monoidal unit: e_H = \varrho_\Phi \circ \bigl(t^{-1}\varrho_\Phi^*\bigr) with t = \mathrm{tr}_F(\varrho_\Phi^* \cdot \varrho_\Phi), and \varrho_\Phi^* \cdot \varrho_\Phi = t \cdot \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{1}}. Cyclicity of the trace gives \mathrm{tr}_F(e_H) = \mathrm{tr}_F(\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{1}}), which is 1 for a unit-normalised cyclic trace. The value [2]_q of (G-2) is the q-dimension of all of A^{(H)}, not the trace of its rank-one image.

The closed form for \mathcal{N}_{\rm sym}(q)

Writing \mathrm{tr}_F(e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW} \cdot e_H) as \dim_q of the image of e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW} on A^{(W^+)} \oplus A^{(W^-)} \oplus A^{(Z)} times \dim_q(e_H \cdot A^{(H)}), and then multiplying the per-host dimensions, is not justified, for two reasons.

  1. q-dimension is additive over direct sums and multiplicative over tensor products. (G-1) makes A^{(W^+)}, A^{(W^-)}, A^{(Z)} and A^{(H)} direct summands of A, so the q-dimension of their direct sum is the sum of the per-host values, not their product.
  2. The trace of a composite of idempotents is not in general a product of traces. If e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW} and e_H are idempotents of A supported on the orthogonal summands of (G-1), then e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW} \cdot e_H = 0. A non-zero value of \mathrm{tr}_F(e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW} \cdot e_H) therefore needs the two idempotents to act on different tensor factors, which (G-1) does not supply.

The corpus does not settle which object is meant. Two readings are recorded, and neither is selected.

  • Reading (a), tensor product. The electroweak host is A^{(W^+)} \otimes A^{(W^-)} \otimes A^{(Z)}, the Higgs host A^{(H)} is a further tensor factor, and \mathrm{tr}_F is multiplicative on e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW} \otimes e_H. Then, with (G-2) and (G-4),
  \mathcal{N}_{\rm sym}^{(a)}(q)
  \;=\;
  [4]_q \cdot [4]_q \cdot [6]_q \cdot 1
  \;=\;
  [4]_q^2 \, [6]_q.

This reading needs a tensor structure on the hosts that (G-1) does not state.

  • Reading (b), direct sum, as (G-1) states. The q-dimension of the symmetric-channel image is additive over the summands:
  \dim_q\!\bigl(e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW}\bigl[A^{(W^+)} \oplus A^{(W^-)} \oplus A^{(Z)}\bigr]\bigr)
  \;=\;
  2\,[4]_q + [6]_q,

taking e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW} to act as the identity on each host, as (G-2) assumes. Keeping the outer factor \dim_q(e_H \cdot A^{(H)}) = \mathrm{tr}_F(e_H) = 1 gives \mathcal{N}_{\rm sym}^{(b)}(q) = 2\,[4]_q + [6]_q. By point 2 this is not \mathrm{tr}_F(e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW} \cdot e_H). It is the q-dimension of the symmetric-channel image, and the composition rule that would turn it into the trace is not specified.

  • What the trace algebra decides. For any additive, cyclic, unit-normalised trace, the composite reading of \mathrm{tr}_F(e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW}\cdot e_H) is a vacuum expectation value. Because e_H factors through \mathbf{1}, \mathrm{tr}_F(f\circ e_H) = t^{-1}\langle\varrho_\Phi^*, f\,\varrho_\Phi\rangle for every endomorphism f of the host of e_H. When f is an idempotent commuting with e_H this value is 0 or 1, and it is 0 when f and e_H live on different summands. The dimension of the electroweak host never enters. A q-dimension-valued \mathcal{N}_{\rm sym} therefore needs the product to be the tensor product e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW}\otimes e_H, on a tensor power of A rather than on A, and then \mathcal{N}_{\rm sym} = \mathrm{tr}_F(e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW}). The trace is additive on direct sums and multiplicative on tensor products, so it cannot decide between (a) and (b): that is a question about the host object.
  • What the rest of the corpus fixes. Neither reading matches the host structure used elsewhere. In the Hoefsmit realisation, distinct carriers are tensor factors: W, Z and T(2,8) act on disjoint strand pairs, in H_2(q)^{\otimes 3} \subset H_6(q). There is a single W slot. The charge–spin theorem gives W^- the swap-image a_{W^-} = a_{W^+}^{-1}, so the two sector vectors are negatives of each other and span one line. W^+ and W^- are therefore neither two tensor factors, as (a) assumes, nor two independent summands, as (b) counts. Table 1 agrees, listing them as the T^\pm weight spaces of one adjoint. Taking (G-2) and (G-4) as given, this structure gives [4]_q\,[6]_q \approx 26.25 at q_0, conditional on the torus-link identification. It does not justify (G-2) itself: the slot object is V \otimes V with \dim_q = [2]_q^2 = [3]_q + 1, while [4]_q and [6]_q are \dim_q V_{3/2} and \dim_q V_{5/2}, which are not among the representations of Table 1. They come from crossing counts, not from a q-dimension the corpus derives.

The factor 1 in both readings is (G-4): e_H factors through \mathbf{1} (the Higgs vacuum-residual idempotent). The host labels T(2,4) and T(2,6) of (G-2) come from the electroweak/Higgs torus-link identification, which is itself a conjecture. See Table 2.

The value on the strand-pair slots

Suppose the hosts of (G-1) are the strand pairs of the Hoefsmit realisation: W, Z and H act on the strand pairs (1,2), (3,4), (5,6) of V^{\otimes 6}, with carriers \sigma_1^4, \sigma_3^6, \sigma_5^8. Call this hypothesis (H1). The labels W, Z, H come from the torus-link identification, so (H1) is conditional on that conjecture, and (G-1) as stated, a direct sum, does not imply it. Under (H1) and a choice of trace, stated in step 3, the value of \mathcal{N}_{\rm sym} is forced:

  1. Each carrier \sigma_i^{2k} has exactly the two eigenvalues q^{2k} and q^{-2k}, and its spectral projectors are the projectors e^{+}, e^{-} of \sigma_i itself, for every k. So e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW} is e^{+} on the W and Z slots.
  2. By (G-3), e_H factors through \mathbf{1}. On a slot V \otimes V the invariant line is the -q^{-1} eigenline of \sigma_5, which is one-dimensional, so e_H = e^{-}(\sigma_5), with \mathrm{tr}_F(e_H) = 1 as (G-4) requires. The identification of the invariants with that eigenline is quantum Schur–Weyl duality [jimbo1986].
  3. Take \mathrm{tr}_F to be a multiple of the pivotal trace; call this (H4). A general cyclic trace takes independent values on e^{+} and e^{-}, and \mathrm{tr}_F(e_H) = 1 fixes only the value on e^{-}. Under (H4) that condition selects the unnormalised pivotal trace, whose Markov parameter is q^3/(q^2+1).
  4. On V^{\otimes 6} the composite e_{\rm sym}^{\rm EW} \cdot e_H is the tensor product e^{+} \otimes e^{+} \otimes e^{-}, and the trace is multiplicative over slots.

Since \mathrm{tr}_F(e^{+}) = [3]_q on each slot,

  \mathcal{N}_{\rm sym}(q) \;=\; [3]_q^2, \qquad \mathcal{N}_{\rm sym}(q_0) \approx 9.2641 .

This is none of readings (a) and (b) and differs from the slot value [4]_q\,[6]_q above, which took (G-2) as given. Under (H1), (G-2) does not hold: the symmetric image of every carrier is the adjoint V_1, of q-dimension [3]_q for each k, which is the adjoint of Table 1, and not V_{k-1/2} of q-dimension [2k]_q. The idempotent e_H = e^{-}(\sigma_5) is the alternating eigenprojector, whereas the torus-link identification places H in the bar-even part A_+ of \sigma_5^8, a grading component rather than a spectral projector; the two descriptions are not reconciled.

The anchor value is not a host trace

The anchor value \mathcal{N}_{\rm sym}(q_0) \approx 213.11 is defined as N_v / \prod_{k=2,3,4} [2k]_q^2/[2]_q, with N_v = v/(E_\times \mu_0). Writing it through the weak scale v/m_p of the torus-link identification gives the identity

  \mathcal{N}_{\rm sym}^{\rm anchor} \;=\; 3\,\frac{m_p}{m_e}\cdot\frac{v}{m_p}\cdot\frac{[2]_q^3}{\bigl([4]_q\,[6]_q\,[8]_q\bigr)^2}.

The factor 3\,m_p/m_e \approx 5508 is the proton mass counted in crossings; the remaining factor is \approx 0.03869. Every q-dimension in \mathbf{Rep}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)) is a non-negative integer combination of q-integers and is finite at q = 1. So no host trace equals the anchor as a function of q, and agreement at the single point q_0 would be a coincidence of evaluation, not an identification.   • Force generators (T_{3,4}, T_{3,5}, T_{2,9}) populate the H^{0,1} antiholomorphic sector. The composite winding 9 = 3 \times 3 of T_{2,9} factors through T_{2,3}. The knot T_{3,4} provides Hopf-squared color binding. The knot T_{3,5} carries three-strand colour at the second-generation column; the production reading below identifies it with the gg \to c\bar{c} vertex rather than a weak mediator.

A generator whose winding interpolates three matter copies binds rather than acts as a standalone particle. This yields the identification:

  T_{2,9} \longleftrightarrow \text{strong force (gluonic binding)}.

The 9 crossings of T_{2,9} provide exactly three crossing triples, one per color tube. In the Borromean baryon, the three color fibers thread the three quark components. As their three-fold cover, T_{2,9} supplies the topological rigidity that holds the configuration together. The zero hyperbolic volume of T_{2,9} aligns with massless gluons.

The structure of T_{3,5}.

The torus knot T_{3,5} has 3-strand meridional winding. This places it in the force carrier family alongside T_{3,4}. Its longitudinal winding n = 5 matches T_{2,5} (muon, charm). This creates a cross-link between the two winding families:

m \backslash n 3 4 5 7 9
2 e^-, u — \mu, c \tau, b^{\sigma} force
3 — force force — —

The knot T_{3,5} sits at the intersection of the m = 3 (quark) row and the n = 5 (second-generation) column. Its knot group relation x^3 = y^5 intertwines the three-strand color structure with five-fold longitudinal winding.

If T_{2,9} carries the strong force, T_{3,5} is the natural candidate for a flavor-changing interaction. It topologically connects the m = 2 and m = 3 families. The weak force changes quark flavor (e.g., u \leftrightarrow d via W^{\pm}) and requires precisely this cross-family mediation. Alternatively, T_{3,5} encodes the electroweak mixing between leptonic and quark sectors.

Production reading: T_{3,5} as the gg \to c\bar{c} vertex. The pair-production mechanism sharpens the T_{3,5} reading and disfavours the weak-mediator alternative above. Dominant second-generation quark production is gluon fusion gg \to c\bar{c}; the two incoming gluons occupy the three-strand colour (m = 3) sector — the sector of the strong generator T_{2,9} — and the Frobenius Gram matrix selects the emergent pair by the colour-tube threading operation, which attaches the m = 3 colour structure to the second-generation longitudinal winding n = 5. On this reading T_{3,5} is the production vertex, and the second-generation quark is its coloured outgoing leg: a colour-threaded T_{2,5}. The uncoloured T_{2,5} is the generation label the quark shares with the muon; T_{3,5} is its coloured realisation under threading. This reading is more consistent than the weak-mediator guess, which collides with the electroweak-triplet assignment W = T_{2,4} — the charged weak boson is a genus-zero torus link, not T_{3,5}. It also reconciles the Standard-Model appendix, where the quark masses are open precisely because quarks carry no independent knot: the second-generation quark is a threaded constituent leg, not a standalone carrier. The identification fixes a channel, not a mass — T_{3,5} has zero hyperbolic volume, so a second-generation quark mass requires the complex-volume constituent functional (the real part of \mathrm{Vol} + i\,\mathrm{CS} projected onto the n = 5 Frobenius block), which is open.

Summary of candidate assignments.

Generator Structure Candidate Rationale
T_{2,9} Three-fold cover of T_{2,3} Strong force / gluonic binding Interpolates 3 color copies of the trefoil; zero volume = massless
T_{3,5} Cross-link of m = 3, n = 5 gg \to c\bar{c} vertex / second-generation quark channel Colour-threaded T_{2,5}; weak-mediator reading disfavoured by W = T_{2,4}

Open problem. Make the force interpretation precise. Identify T_{2,9} and T_{3,5} with specific gauge bosons (gluon, W^{\pm}, Z^0). Compute their Skein interaction terms with matter generators. Compare coupling constants derived from the mass functional with Standard Model values.
prose:intro-confined-particles-shells: Having classified individual leptons, mesons, Borromean baryons, and the electroweak even-twist torus-link triplet \{T(2,4), T(2,6), T(2,8)\}, one turns to composite multi-particle states. The Frobenius positivity condition on the Iwahori–Hecke algebra stratifies confined composites into principal shells: a state at confinement level \ell occupies the \ell-th shell precisely when the Frobenius form on its active Wedderburn support is positive definite. This section defines the confinement category, its Markov functor, and the dressing morphisms that assemble multi-electron and multi-nucleon shells.
def:confined-particle:
Definition Confined particle. A confined particle is a tuple

  P \;=\; (\mathrm{name},\ \ell,\ [K]_M,\ n_0)

where:

  1. \mathrm{name} is a symbol drawn from a fixed registry of particle shortcuts.
  2. \ell \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0} is the confinement level (quark = 0, nucleon = 1, atom = 2, molecule/compound = 3, \ldots).
  3. [K]_M is the Markov-equivalence class of a closed braid K. It is represented canonically by the Gröbner–Shirshov normal form of its associated Hecke element T_w \in H_{n_0}(q).
  4. n_0 is the coarse strand count at level \ell: the minimal number of strands needed to express K as a closed braid at its own level.

The class [K]_M is not intrinsically confined at any particular q. Confinement is a q-indexed predicate \mathrm{confined}(P, q) that holds if and only if the matrix Frobenius PSD cone admits a feasible \Phi^* \succeq 0. A confined particle is stable at q if and only if it is additionally Frobenius-non-degenerate there. Unstable species are confined particles for all q in the generic locus even though their decay channels are open.

Canonical representative. Among all closed-braid words in [K]_M, one chooses the one with the shortlex-minimal Gröbner–Shirshov normal form as the canonical representative \mathrm{GS}(P). One computes the witness data k_{\max}(P, q) on this representative. Two particles are equal if and only if their names are equal, which occurs if and only if \mathrm{GS}(P_1) = \mathrm{GS}(P_2).

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs. Any generic categorical identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
ex:confined-particle-examples:
Example Confined particles across levels: quark to compound. Examples.

  • quark: \ell = 0, n_0 = 1, [K]_M = [\sigma_0] in H_1(q).
  • neutrino: \ell = 0, n_0 = 1, [K]_M = [\mathbf{1}] (unknot 0_1, no crossings). Confined and stable at q_0; the Frobenius-PSD cone is satisfied since \Phi^* = \mathbf{1} \succeq 0.
  • photon: \ell = 0, n_0 = 4, [K]_M = [\mathbf{1}_{B_4}] (four-strand identity in B_4, no crossings). Confined at q_0 via the Reeb-bundle holonomy.
  • proton: \ell = 1, n_0 = 3, [K]_M = [B_3(\mathrm{uud})] with crossing types (pp, pn, pn).
  • neutron: \ell = 1, n_0 = 3, [K]_M = [B_3(\mathrm{udd})].
  • electron: \ell = 1, n_0 = 2, [K]_M = [\sigma_1^3] (trefoil 3_1).
  • He4: \ell = 2, n_0 = 4 nucleons, [K]_M determined by the canonical ILP ground-state configuration for (Z,N)=(2,2).
  • benzene: \ell = 3, n_0 = 6 atom-strands.
def:confinement-category:
Definition The confinement category \mathbf{Conf} has:

  • Objects: confined particles P at every level \ell \ge 0.
  • Morphisms: structure-preserving maps organised into three families:
Family Symbol Action
Unfolding \uparrow_\ell Replace each level-\ell strand by its level-(\ell-1) constituent braid
Folding \downarrow_\ell Quotient a subbraid at level \ell-1 to a single level-\ell strand
Dressing \mathrm{dress} Extend H_n(R, q) \hookrightarrow H_{n+m}(q) and attach m additional strands via an SDP-feasible binding subword
  • Composition: concatenation of Hecke-algebra embeddings. One right-composes \mathrm{dress} with \uparrow_\ell and \downarrow_\ell.
  • Identity: the identity embedding \mathrm{id}_P: H_{n_0}(q) \hookrightarrow H_{n_0}(q).
rem:confinement-category-invertibility: Remark Invertibility of the morphisms of \mathbf{Conf}. In the confinement category, unfolding and folding are mutually inverse when restricted to particles whose coarse representation captures the full partition content. The morphism \mathrm{dress} is generally not invertible because the binding subword may not be uniquely reversible.
rem:confinement-category-markov-functor:
Remark Functoriality of the Markov trace on \mathbf{Conf}. Functoriality of the Markov trace. The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M extends to a functor

  \mathrm{tr}_M: \mathbf{Conf} \to \mathbb{C}(q)

sending every confined particle to its trace value and every morphism to the induced trace transformation. The trace \mathrm{tr}_M is invariant under \uparrow_\ell and \downarrow_\ell. Under \mathrm{dress}, it multiplies by the binding weight determined by the active support.
ex:confinement-category-atomic-chain: Example The atomic chain in \mathbf{Conf}. The chain \mathrm{quark} \xrightarrow{\downarrow_1} \mathrm{nucleon} \xrightarrow{\downarrow_2} \mathrm{atom} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{dress}} \mathrm{neutral\ atom} \xrightarrow{\downarrow_3} \mathrm{molecule} is a composite morphism in \mathbf{Conf} taking free quarks to a bonded molecule by successive foldings and one dressing. Each arrow preserves or extends the Markov trace.
def:dressed-particle:
Definition Dressed particle via shell-attachment morphism. Let P_{\mathrm{bare}} be a confined particle at level \ell. Let S = (\{e_k\}, \iota, W_{\mathrm{bind}}) be an electron shell of multiplicity Z attached to it. The dressing morphism at S is the arrow in the confinement category:

  \mathrm{dress}_S\,:\;P_{\mathrm{bare}}\;\longrightarrow\;P_{\mathrm{dressed}}

This morphism sends P_{\mathrm{bare}} to the dressed particle:

  P_{\mathrm{dressed}}
  \;=\;
  \bigl(
    \mathrm{name}(P_{\mathrm{bare}}) \oplus \mathrm{name}(S),\;
    \ell,\;
    [\iota(K_{\mathrm{bare}}) \cdot W_{\mathrm{bind}}]_M,\;
    n_0 + Z
  \bigr)

Here \mathrm{name}(S) is the shell label, [\ \cdot\ ]_M denotes Markov equivalence, and the composite braid lives in H_{n_0 + Z}(q) via the cabling embedding.
ex:dressed-particle-examples:
Example Dressing bare nuclei to neutral atoms. Examples.

  • Bare proton \xrightarrow{\mathrm{dress}_{[1s^1]}} neutral hydrogen {}^1\mathrm{H}.
  • Bare ^4He-nucleus \xrightarrow{\mathrm{dress}_{[1s^2]}} neutral helium (noble gas, Z = 2).
  • Bare ^{20}Ne-nucleus \xrightarrow{\mathrm{dress}_{[1s^2 2s^2 2p^6]}} neutral neon (noble gas, Z = 10).
rem:dressed-particle-properties:
Remark Composition, stability, and Markov-trace functoriality of dressing. Composition. Dressing is not generally invertible. Stripping electrons changes the binding subword via the SDP. However, dressings compose:

  \mathrm{dress}_{S_2} \circ \mathrm{dress}_{S_1}
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{dress}_{S_1 \oplus S_2}

Here \oplus concatenates shell data when the combined Z remains SDP-feasible. Partial dressing (0 < Z' < Z_{\max}) yields ions.

Stability under dressing. The Frobenius-stability index of P_{\mathrm{dressed}} is monotonically non-decreasing along the dressing chain toward closed-shell noble-gas configurations (Z \in \{2, 10, 18, 36, 54, 86\}). Each shell closure is a \mu \ge 2 multi-operator fixed point of the SDP. Breaking the bond requires simultaneously breaking every tight dual block. Noble-gas objects are therefore local terminal objects of the dressing sub-diagram of \mathbf{Conf}.

Functoriality of the Markov trace. Under dressing, the Markov trace transforms as:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(P_{\mathrm{dressed}})
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M(P_{\mathrm{bare}}) \cdot
  \prod_{\lambda \in \mathcal{S}^*(S, q)} w_\lambda^{\,\langle \pi_\lambda, \Phi^* \rangle}

Here \mathcal{S}^*(S, q) is the SDP active support and w_\lambda are the block shadow prices. For \mu(S, q) = 1, this collapses to the scalar-LP product. For \mu \ge 2, the full matrix shadow contributes.

Typical bare particle. In the dressing morphism the bare particle P_{\mathrm{bare}} is typically a bare nucleus, at level \ell = 2.
prose:intro-atom-isotope-knots: Every neutral atom or isotope (Z, N) is represented by a canonical closed braid in H_{3(Z+N)}(q) formed by embedding Z proton and N neutron Borromean blocks along the inter-nucleon connector permutation w_{\mathrm{inter}}. This section proves the existence and uniqueness of the normal-form representative T_w via the Diamond Lemma for the Hecke algebra, establishes decidability of the integer-linear-programming stability predicate, and defines the unstable atoms for which it fails.
def:atom-knot:
Definition Atom as a knot via Gröbner normal form. An atom of type (Z, N) is a closed braid K whose Gröbner–Shirshov normal form in H_{n(K)}(q) admits a block decomposition:

  T_w
  \;=\;
  T_{w_{q^Z}} \;\cdot\; T_{w_{\bar q^N}} \;\cdot\; T_{w_{\mathrm{inter}}},
  \qquad
  w \;=\; w_{q^Z} \cdot w_{\bar q^N} \cdot w_{\mathrm{inter}}
  \;\in\; S_{n(K)}.

The components are:

  • n(K) is the braid index of K. For a (Z, N) atom built from Borromean baryons on 3 strands each plus inter-nucleon connectors, n(K) = 3(Z+N).
  • w_{q^Z} \in S_{n(K)} is the proton-quark block. It is the product of Z permutations. Each permutation realizes the Borromean baryon normal form for one \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d} proton-quark substructure on a disjoint 3-strand block.
  • w_{\bar q^N} is the neutron-quark block. It consists of N disjoint Borromean normal forms for \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d} neutron-quark substructures.
  • w_{\mathrm{inter}} is the inter-nucleon connector. This permutation realizes the pp, nn, and pn crossings between the Z + N disjoint baryon blocks.

The atom is a knot. The atom is the closed braid \hat K = \hat\beta obtained via the Markov closure of any braid representative \beta that realizes T_w.
rem:atom-knot-remark:
Remark The atom-knot is a topological object. The block decomposition of an atom is unique up to normal form rewriting; no positional or temporal ordering is imposed beyond the shortlex-canonical normal form.

Markov-trace invariance guarantees that the closure \hat K forms a well-defined knot or link in S^3. No phase or temperature data enters the definition. The atom represents a purely topological object.

Phase, dynamics, and evolution represent separate structures defined on the space of atom-knots. The same atom K may exhibit different confinement levels at different q, but K itself remains independent of q.
prop:atom-knot-exists: Proposition Existence of the atom-knot for any (Z, N). For any pair (Z, N) \in \mathbb{N}_{\geq 0}^2 with Z + N \geq 1, the atom-knot of type (Z, N) exists as a closed braid in H_{3(Z+N)}(q) on the generic locus.
prf:atom-knot-exists:
Proof Proof of atom knot exists. One constructs the normal form (NF) T_w \in H_{3(Z+N)}(q) explicitly.

On the intra-nucleon blocks, each Borromean baryon (borromean baryon) possesses a canonical normal form in H_3(R, q) on three strands; let T_p, T_n \in H_3(R, q) denote the proton and neutron normal forms. Under the block-diagonal inclusion, the disconnected tensor product T_p^{\otimes Z} \otimes T_n^{\otimes N} \in H_3(R, q)^{\otimes (Z+N)} embeds into the many-body algebra H_{3(Z+N)}(q) on the intra-nucleon strands.

To couple the individual baryon blocks, let w_{\mathrm{inter}} \in S_{3(Z+N)} be the inter-nucleon connector permutation that realizes the pp, nn, and pn crossings between adjacent baryon blocks (atomic braid crossing table). Multiplying the intra-nucleon embedding by the connector yields the element T_w = T_{w_{q^Z}} \cdot T_{w_{\bar q^N}} \cdot T_{w_{\mathrm{inter}}} \in H_{3(Z+N)}(q), whose Markov closure \hat\beta = \hat T_w forms a closed braid in S^3.

By the Diamond Lemma for the Hecke algebra (hecke normal form), the reduced normal form T_w is independent of the choice of reduction sequence, so the atom-knot is uniquely defined. \square
prop:atom-knot-unique:
Proposition Uniqueness of the atom-knot up to Markov equivalence. Suppose \beta_1 and \beta_2 are two braids in B_{n(K)} that both realize the normal form block decomposition T_w = T_{w_{q^Z}} \cdot T_{w_{\bar q^N}} \cdot T_{w_{\mathrm{inter}}}, that is, they have the same image in the Hecke algebra H_{n(K)}(q). Then their Markov closures have the same Markov trace:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\hat\beta_1) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(\hat\beta_2).

Isotopy of the closures is not claimed: braids with equal Hecke images can close to non-isotopic links, since the Markov trace is the HOMFLY-PT polynomial and that does not separate links (mutant pairs).
prf:atom-knot-unique:
Proof Proof of atom knot unique. The Markov trace on B_n factors through the Hecke algebra: it is the composite of the quotient map B_n \to H_n(q), \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i, with the Ocneanu trace on H_n(q) (Jones–Markov trace). Two braids with the same image T_w in H_n(q) therefore have the same Markov trace, and the trace of a braid is the invariant of its closure. \square

Scope. The previous version of this proof concluded that the closures are isotopic, treating the Hecke quadratic relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1 as a Reidemeister II move. It is not one: Reidemeister II is \sigma_i \sigma_i^{-1} = 1, which holds already in B_n, while the quadratic relation identifies braids that are not isotopic. Uniqueness of the normal form (Diamond Lemma, hecke normal form) is a statement about H_n(q), not about B_n.
def:isotope-knot:
Definition Isotope as a knot variant of fixed proton block. Two atom-knots K_1, K_2 of types (Z, N_1) and (Z, N_2) with N_1 \neq N_2 are isotopes iff their NF block decompositions agree on the proton-quark block:

  T_{w_1} \;=\; T_{w_{q^Z}} \cdot T_{w_{\bar q^{N_1}}^{(1)}} \cdot T_{w_{\mathrm{inter}}^{(1)}},
  \qquad
  T_{w_2} \;=\; T_{w_{q^Z}} \cdot T_{w_{\bar q^{N_2}}^{(2)}} \cdot T_{w_{\mathrm{inter}}^{(2)}},

with identical w_{q^Z}.
rem:isotope-knot-properties:
Remark Isotopes are knot-distinct with independent stability. Two isotopes are knot-distinct. The Markov closures of T_{w_1} and T_{w_2} generally have different Jones polynomials whenever N_1 \neq N_2. The neutron-quark blocks contribute distinct Hecke generators. Isotopes are distinct knots, not the same knot at different aether parameters.

Stability per isotope is independent. The LP-dual ILP-feasibility is computed on the full NF T_w. This includes the w_{\bar q^N} and w_{\mathrm{inter}} blocks. Different isotopes can have different stabilities at the same q. This is the categorical analogue of the classical observation that {}^{12}\mathrm{C} is stable while {}^{14}\mathrm{C} is not.

Equivalence relation. The isotope relation is an equivalence on \{\text{atom-knots with fixed } Z\}. The relation is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. The isotope class of K at fixed Z is parameterized by the neutron-quark block w_{\bar q^N} and the inter-nucleon connector w_{\mathrm{inter}}.
prop:isotope-knot-equivalence:
Proposition A reflexive, symmetric, transitive isotope relation is an equivalence. Let \sim be a relation on atom-knots with fixed Z, and assume that \sim is reflexive, symmetric and transitive. Then \sim is an equivalence relation.

Whether the isotope relation of def:isotope-knot satisfies these three properties is not part of this statement; they are hypotheses.
